steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Command words tell you exactly what the examiner expects — misreading them is the most common reason for losing marks

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'Describe' requires a straightforward account of what something is or how it works — give factual detail without analysis or evaluation

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'Explain' requires you to give reasons or show how something works — go beyond description by showing causes, effects or the reasoning behind a legal principle

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'Analyse' requires you to break down a topic into its component parts and examine the relationship between them — identify strengths and weaknesses

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Underline the command word and the focus of the question before you start writing — this keeps your answer on track For evaluation questions, always present both sides before reaching a conclusion — one-sided answers cannot access the top mark bands Use connectives to signal your argument: 'On one hand...', 'However...', 'Furthermore...', 'In conclusion...' For scenario questions, always apply the law to the facts — don't just state legal principles without connecting them to the specific case Plan your 15-mark answer before writing — even 2 minutes of planning produces a more coherent and better-structured response
